title: Microsoft.Extensions.AI: DI and Structured Output
why: In lecture 2 we created `IChatClient` in the Controller with `new`, and the answer was free text — “almost” exact even with few-shot. Today we put the client in the right place (DI and configuration, as in the API course) and force the model to return a C# type instead of text: an enum or an object that goes straight into our existing logic. This is the bridge between a user's free text and our code.
outcomes: Register `IChatClient` in DI with `AddChatClient`: the key in User Secrets, the model in `appsettings.json`
Get an enum with `GetResponseAsync<T>` and explain why it's more reliable than few-shot
Extract an object from text with a `record`: nullable fields, `Description`, today's date in the prompt
Explain why the shape is guaranteed but the content is not, and check the received object in C#

review.q: What's wrong with `new Client().AsIChatClient(...)` inside a Controller, and how do we fix it?
review.a: A new client on every request · the model name is in the code · we can't plug a fake client into a test → `AddChatClient` in `Program.cs` (Singleton) + constructor injection in the Controller

review.q: Where do we keep the Gemini key and where the model name? Why in different places?
review.a: The key — in User Secrets (it's a secret, it must not get into Git; on a server — an environment variable) · the model — in `appsettings.json` (not a secret; change it without changing code)

review.q: How does few-shot differ from structured output?
review.a: Few-shot **asks** for a shape with examples — by probability · structured output **forces** it: a JSON Schema from the C# type goes with the request, the model can't write outside the schema, `.Result` is already a C# type

review.q: Why `int? Guests` and not `int` in `BookingRequest`? And why do we put today's date in the prompt?
review.a: `?` gives the model the right to say “I don't know” (null); with `int` it's forced to write something and will make it up · the model doesn't know today's date (stateless, training date) — we provide it for “tomorrow”

review.q: Structured output gave us a `BookingRequest`. Can we write it straight to the database?
review.a: No · the shape is guaranteed, the content isn't: “at 8” → 08:00, the guests are missing (null) · C# checks the fields before the database

quiz.q: Why is it bad to create `IChatClient` with `new` in a Controller field?
options: The Controller is created on every request — and with it a new client and HTTP connection
A client created with `new` can't call Gemini
The key costs more that way
quiz.explain: ASP.NET Core creates the Controller anew for every request. Besides, the model name is in the code and we can't plug a fake client into a test.

quiz.q: With what lifetime does `AddChatClient` register `IChatClient` by default?
options: Transient — a new one every time
Singleton — one for the whole application
quiz.explain: The client holds HTTP connections and is thread-safe, so one is enough for the whole application.

quiz.q: Where do we keep the Gemini API key during development?
options: As a const in the Controller
quiz.explain: User Secrets are stored outside the project and don't get into Git. `appsettings.json` and `launchSettings.json` go to Git.

quiz.q: We want OpenAI instead of Gemini. Which file changes?
options: Only `Program.cs` — the line that creates the client (and the package)
quiz.explain: The Controllers know only `IChatClient`. The provider is created in one place — `Program.cs`. Switching to another Gemini model is only `appsettings.json`.

quiz.q: The few-shot classify sometimes returns `Search.`. Why doesn't this happen with `GetResponseAsync<RequestType>`?
options: The JSON Schema goes with the request and the model can't choose a token outside the schema
quiz.explain: Few-shot asks for a shape, structured output forces it. The allowed values are in the schema, and the model chooses only among them.

options: A `string` we must convert by hand
quiz.explain: `ChatResponse<T>` is a normal `ChatResponse` (with tokens and the finish reason) plus `Result`.

quiz.q: The endpoint returns `Ok(response.Result)` where `Result` = `Sentiment.Mixed`. What do we see in Swagger?
options: `2` — by default ASP.NET Core returns an enum as a number
quiz.explain: That's why on the slide we return `sentiment.ToString()`. The alternative is `JsonStringEnumConverter` in `Program.cs`.

quiz.q: “There are four of us, tomorrow at 8” — why do we write `Today is {DateTime.Now:…}` in the system prompt?
options: The answer is faster that way
The model doesn't know today's date — we provide it so it can work out “tomorrow”
Gemini returns an error without a date
It's part of the JSON Schema
quiz.explain: The model is stateless and its knowledge stops at its training date. Today's date is context we provide — with the lecture 2 prompt template.

quiz.q: If `BookingRequest` had `int Guests` (without `?`) and the text had no number, what would most likely happen?
options: The model would return an error
The model would make up a number (e.g. 2) — the schema forces it to write a number
quiz.explain: The schema says “a number goes here”, and the model is forced to write one. `int?` also allows null in the schema — “I don't know”.

quiz.q: Structured output returned a `BookingRequest`. What is guaranteed?
options: That the answer has the shape of `BookingRequest`; C# has to check the values
That `At` is always within opening hours
quiz.explain: The shape is guaranteed, the content is not: “at 8” may become 08:00, a field may be null. C# checks before the database.

quiz.q: In a structured output prompt, is it better to write “return JSON with fields at and guests”?
options: No — the schema is sent with the request anyway; in the prompt we write what to extract and by which rules
Yes, otherwise the model can't write JSON
quiz.explain: Google recommends not repeating the schema in the prompt — it lowers quality. The schema sets the shape, the prompt sets the rules (e.g. “leave null whatever is not in the text”).

summary: **`AddChatClient`** — `IChatClient` is created once in `Program.cs` and registered in DI as a Singleton. The Controller receives it **through the constructor** — like `DbContext` in the API course.
**The key** — in User Secrets (`dotnet user-secrets set "Gemini:ApiKey" "..."`), **the model** — in `appsettings.json`. Another model = configuration only, another provider = `Program.cs` only.
**`GetResponseAsync<T>`** — a JSON Schema is created from the C# type, sent with the request, and the model can't write outside it. `response.Result` is already a `T`.
**enum** — one value from a list (classification); **record** — several fields from text (extraction). Nullable fields and “leave null” — so it doesn't make things up; today's date — in the prompt.
**The shape is guaranteed, the content is not.** C# checks the received object before the database.
